- At x, I have the highest priority (rank 1)
- At z, I also have the highest priority (rank 1)
- At y, I'm lower priority (rank 2)
- At w, I'm lower priority (rank 2)

Given that most applicants seem to favor y > x > w > z, competition will be high at y and x. My top priority status at x and z gives me an advantage.

Since x is my most preferred school and I have top priority there, I'll rank x first. z is my next most preferred school where I also have top priority, so I'll rank it second.

y is third, as it's less preferred and I have lower priority. w is last, being my least preferred school with low priority.
